Anya: Quick heads-up — during a FP8+INT8 mixed-kernel canary (calib-2026-03-15-A) we started seeing sporadic NaN/INF in token outputs for very long prompts (>6k). Repro locally with kv-rescale path enabled.

Matt: Oh no. Any pprof/flamegraph links?

Anya: Put a snapshot here (internal): https://perf.redwood.internal/runs/calib-2026-03-15-A
Profiler excerpt pasted:
``
kernel_selector: chosen=int8_matmul_fast layer=24 dense_ms=0.83
kv_cache: rescale_applied=1.000e+02 kv_accum=1.2e+04
runtime: detected inf in output tensor at step=412
```
Repro code (toy):
``
for i in range(5000):
  out = runtime.generate(prompt, max_new_tokens=8)
  if torch.isinf(out).any():
    print('inf at iter', i)
    break
```

Olga: Hypotheses:
- smoothquant per-channel calib created very small scales for some channels -> combined with int8 matmul causes overflow
- KV-cache rescale factor looks huge (100x) in that run -> may amplify activations
Short mitigations: clip activations before writing KV and clamp per-layer scales.

Sam: Also saw a big burst in batching logs: 16 reqs got merged with mixed seq-lens. Mixed-length batches cause longer cumulative attention ops and some kernels assume narrower dynamic ranges. Short-term: lower max_batch_delay or enforce seq-len bucketing.

Kevin: Can you attach quant metadata and kernel selection hints? I'll add a numeric-sanitizer hook to check for NaN/Inf after matmul and fall back to fp16/fp8 kernels if triggered. We should also log per-batch kernel decisions.

Anya: Quant metadata:
``
quant_meta: model=v3.1.2, calib_mode=smoothquant, alpha=0.03, per_channel=True
kernel_hint: prefer=int8 when tokens<2048 else fp8
```
I'll run a focused repro forcing identical batch selection and upload pprofs.

perf-bot: [ALERT] perf-regression: tail latency +35% for model v3.1.2 on run calib-2026-03-15-A. Threshold=+15%.

ci-bot: CI: PR #4827 numeric-sanitizer RFC - unit tests passed (linux, cuda12, int8-kernels).

Olga: Quick experiment plan (config patch):
``
runtime.kernel_fallback:
  - when: detects_inf
    action: fallback_fp16
runtime.kv_clamp:
  enabled: true
  clamp_value: 1e2
batching:
  split_by_seq_len: true
  max_batch_delay_ms: 8  # lowered from 20
```
I'll run a calibration sweep with smaller smoothquant alpha (0.015) and add explicit clip_threshold=20. Will measure perplexity/regression vs perf.

Matt: Suggested rollout steps:
1) Abort the canary (calib-2026-03-15-A) — stop traffic.
2) Deploy numeric-sanitizer + fallback in staging (Kevin).
3) Run Olga's calibration sweep and full perf+quality evals.
4) Enforce seq-len bucketed batching until validated.
5) If infs persist, disable int8 kernels for long sequences by default.

Kevin: Landing sanitizer RFC now; will add a hot path to fallback without full restart. Hoping to hotfix staging today.

Anya: I'll upload repro traces and assign follow-ups to Kevin/Olga. Scheduling a 1h sync in #eng-runtime at 16:00 PT. :thumbsup:

Sam: Also flagged infra to print kernel-selector per-batch reason codes via a small debug flag. That should help correlate kernel decision -> numeric event.

Matt: Good. Keep updates here and paste perf deltas after abort.

Olga: Note for the calibration sweep: track both generation quality (logprobs/perp) and numeric stability metrics (#inf, #nan, max_abs_activation) per-layer. We might trade a few pps for stability.

Anya: Agreed. Also adding a runtime metric: kv_rescale_factor distribution per-write. If we see long tails we can clamp in the write path.

Kevin: One more idea — add optional stochastic clamping when writing KV for int8 path (random clamp within [v/2, v]) to avoid pathological channel extremes during long recurrences. Will prototype.

Matt: Thanks everyone. If anyone hits a hard repro, drop the exact seed/prompt here so we can correlate.

perf-bot: Canary aborted by Matt at 1919990200. Traffic diverted.

Anya: Repro trace uploaded + pprof link: https://perf.redwood.internal/traces/1919990001

Sam: Reminder: test should include bursty production-like batching pattern (mixed seq-lens + spikes) — synthetic single-request tests miss the batching interactions.

Kevin: Working on sanitizer + fallback; will post PR and staging perf numbers when ready.

Matt: Closing loop: once sanitizer lands, we re-run canary with seq-len bucketing and smaller smoothquant alpha. If perf delta < +10% and no NaNs, promote.

Anya: Thanks. Assigning follow-ups: Kevin (sanitizer + fallback), Olga (calib sweep + clips), Sam (batching flags + kernel logs).
